::: {#exm-fwer}
#### FWER of unadjusted testing in the simulated family

Repeat the simulation of @exm-rejection-counts 2000 times,
rejecting every null hypothesis with $p_j \le 0.05$ each time,
and record the fraction of repetitions with at least one false positive:

```{r}
#| label: fwer-unadjusted
#| code-fold: false
run_simulation <- function(reject_fn, reps = 2000) {
  replicate(reps, {
    sim <- simulate_tests()
    count_outcomes(reject_fn(sim$p), sim$is_null)
  })
}

set.seed(572)
sim_counts <- list()
sim_counts$unadjusted <- run_simulation(function(p) p <= 0.05)
fwer_unadjusted <- mean(sim_counts$unadjusted["V", ] >= 1)
fwer_unadjusted
```

The estimated FWER is `r round(fwer_unadjusted, 3)`:
with 900 true null hypotheses,
almost every repetition produces a false positive,
as @thm-false-positive-prob predicts for tests that are independent.
:::
